expectations.text: Recognizes conversion rate is a LAGGING, live-traffic outcome whose per-round verification is a slow, noisy experiment not available at agent-loop timescale, so the atom is not cheaper to verify than to produce
expectations.evidence: It states 'Conversion is a slow, noisy, statistical signal. Reading a real lift takes weeks of live traffic and a significance test — no agent round can observe it' and calls the win-atom 'undecidable inside the loop,' directly capturing that verification is not available at loop timescale and thus not cheaper than production.

expectations.text: Does NOT set up an autonomous convergence loop that treats 'conversion improved' as a fast, per-round checkable atom
expectations.evidence: It explicitly says 'don't build the loop you're describing,' moves agents onto decidable atoms (grounded hypothesis, shippable instrumented variant), and states '"Done" for an item means live-test-ready and correctly measured — explicitly not "wins"' with the win/lose verdict handed to a calendar-paced A/B platform.

expectations.text: Distinguishes the true outcome (conversion) from fast proxies (perf/Lighthouse, accessibility, a concrete design rubric) and, if it proposes looping on a proxy, explicitly flags it as a gameable proxy that can diverge from the real goal
expectations.evidence: It uses axe/Lighthouse (a11y + perf/LCP) and Playwright only as regression guardrails rather than the optimization target, keeps conversion as the sole significance-tested verifier, and flags the self-scored 'predicted conversion — i.e. taste' proxy as one that 'drifts, games its own judgment.'

expectations.text: Explains WHY looping directly on the lagging/gameable outcome fails: no ground-truth signal available per round, reward-hacking the proxy, budget burned without real direction
expectations.evidence: It cites all three: 'the loop has nothing external to verify a "win" against' (no ground truth), 'it drifts, games its own judgment, and hands you a confident green number' (reward hacking), and 'would burn budget producing plausible-looking redesigns that no one has shown convert better' (wasted budget).
